title: Keep DTO mappers in the integration layer

facts.note: Bun realization of the core DTO-mapper obligation.
Layer comes from the path's layer segment; files with no layer segment are out of scope.

Needs an AST scan of all in-scope files (not only the diff) that detects any declared function named to*DTO, from*DTO or map*DTO* outside integration — existing, added, moved or changed declarations alike. bun_clean_architecture_detector provides this at verify time.
Advisory hint only: raises attention when writing code; never a prerequisite for activation. The rule fires on the declaration finding whether or not the task mentions these terms.

fires: A to*DTO / from*DTO / map*DTO* function is added in a domain-layer file.
A presentation-layer file declares its own mapper converting a domain entity to a DTO.
An already-existing, unchanged mapper declaration sits in a non-integration layer when the project is verified.
A DTO mapper is moved out of integration into another layer.
doesNotFire: The mapper is declared in an integration-layer file.
The mapper is declared in a test file or a vendored/build directory.
The file carries no layer segment in its path.
Only a bare npm specifier import is involved (outside the project graph).

given: A Bun project file in a layer other than integration contains a function mapping between a DTO and a domain entity (`to*DTO`, `from*DTO`, `map*DTO*`) — whether pre-existing or newly written
when: code is written or the project is verified (all in-scope files are scanned, not only changed ones)
then: Place the DTO mapper in the integration layer, where both the DTO and domain shapes are legitimately visible.
prefer: Keep DTO-to-domain and domain-to-DTO translation in integration.
During GREEN: reuse an existing mapper for the same boundary when one exists.
During GREEN: add only the field mapping the current acceptance requires.
During GREEN: create a new mapper only for a genuinely new boundary translation.
avoid: Placing translation in presentation or domain as a shortcut.
Moving domain behavior into the mapper.
Migrating unrelated mappings while fixing this one.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
why: Mapping is translation across a boundary, which is what integration is for. A mapper in the domain drags the wire format inward; one in presentation duplicates itself once a second caller appears.
evidence: The mapper lives in integration and preserves the intended boundary (no to*DTO/from*DTO/map*DTO* declarations outside integration).
verifier_detail: Flags a DTO-mapper function declared in any layer other than integration (existing declarations included, not only diff additions).
dto_mapper term: a function translating between a DTO and a domain entity, matched by names `to*DTO`, `from*DTO`, `map*DTO*`.
translation_layer term: integration — where a boundary crossing legitimately sees both sides.
Scope: test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned; bare npm specifiers are not layer-checked; files with no layer segment are out of scope, not violations.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
